entities.name: PMID:25088746
observations: Prospective DCCT/EDIC study of 497 people with type 1 diabetes; baseline plasma sphingolipids were measured by HPLC-tandem mass spectrometry and albuminuria was followed for 14–20 years.
At baseline all participants had normal albumin excretion; 141 (28%) developed microalbuminuria and 65 (13%) developed macroalbuminuria.
Higher baseline levels of very-long-chain ceramide species, but not long-chain species, were associated with decreased odds of subsequent macroalbuminuria after multivariable adjustment.
The authors concluded that decreased plasma levels of select ceramide species were associated with development of macroalbuminuria in type 1 diabetes.

entities.name: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
observations: The study population consisted of participants with type 1 diabetes from the DCCT/EDIC cohort.

entities.name: Macroalbuminuria
observations: Macroalbuminuria was defined as albumin excretion rate ≥300 mg/24 h and was the renal outcome most clearly associated with baseline very-long-chain ceramide levels.

entities.name: Very-long-chain ceramides
observations: Baseline plasma very-long-chain ceramide species were measured; increased levels were associated with decreased odds of later macroalbuminuria, implying that decreased levels marked higher nephropathy risk.
